java.say: A has two fields: its own number i, and a link to a B. Through that field, A is coupled to B.
c() is A's own method. It only calls f().
f() is also a method of A. Look at what it uses.
It asks B for j and prints it. It uses nothing of A itself: not i, and no other method of A.
B offers a getter, only so that A can read j. The data is in B, but the work on it is in A. That is low cohesion.
